key_insight: WEST is an open-source, massively parallel excited-state simulation code that combines GW, Bethe-Salpeter, TDDFT, and embedding methods in one framework without explicit virtual-state computations.
engineering_relevance: It enables scalable, high-fidelity prediction of optical and excited-state properties for large materials systems, including perovskites, supporting design and screening workflows.
method: Full-frequency GW, quantum defect embedding theory, BSE, and TDDFT in a common workflow
Avoids explicit virtual electronic states using density functional and density matrix perturbation theory
Uses low-rank dielectric/exact-exchange representations, localization, hierarchical parallelism, and GPU acceleration
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-ideal strong scaling to thousands of GPUs and successful applications to systems with more than a thousand atoms across defects, perovskites, water, and ice.
watch_item: Performance and accuracy depend on advanced parallel/GPU infrastructure and careful implementation of the low-rank and localization approximations.
paper_title: The WEST code for large-scale excited-state materials simulations
